question: Line M serves as the perpendicular bisector of the line segment connecting point J(4, 10) and point K(16, -2). What is the y-intercept of line M?
solution:
**Given:**

Point J = (4, 10)

Point K = (16, −2)

Line M is the perpendicular bisector of JK

**Formula used:**

Midpoint = ((x₁ + x₂) ÷ 2 , (y₁ + y₂) ÷ 2)

Slope = (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁)

Slope of perpendicular line = −1 ÷ slope

Equation of line: y = mx + c

**Calculations:**

⇒ Midpoint of JK

⇒ x = (4 + 16) ÷ 2 = 10

⇒ y = (10 − 2) ÷ 2 = 4

⇒ Midpoint = (10, 4)

⇒ Slope of JK

⇒ (−2 − 10) ÷ (16 − 4) = −12 ÷ 12 = −1

⇒ Slope of line M = 1 (negative reciprocal of −1)

⇒ Equation of line M passing through (10, 4)

⇒ y − 4 = 1(x − 10)

⇒ y = x − 6

⇒ y-intercept when x = 0

⇒ y = −6

**∴ The y-intercept of line M is −6.**
